title: Slow-cooker Swedish meatballs
subtitle: Tender pork and beef meatballs in a creamy gravy
excerpt: Small, tender meatballs made from pork and beef mince, cooked slowly in beef stock and finished with double cream and Dijon mustard. Serve with mashed potato or egg noodles.
sourceNotes: Swedish meatballs, or köttbullar, are a Swedish national dish of pork and beef meatballs served in a cream sauce. The dish became widely known internationally through Swedish furniture retail in the 1990s and 2000s.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the meatballs without the cream sauce for up to 3 months. Make the sauce fresh when reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Meatballs can be made and refrigerated raw for 24 hours before cooking.

content.text: The pork and beef mix gives these meatballs their particular texture: the pork adds fat and moisture, the beef gives depth of flavour. A small amount of whole milk in the mix keeps them tender. The cream sauce is added at the very end to prevent it from splitting during the long cook.

Browning the meatballs before they go in is optional but gives them a better colour in the finished dish. If you skip it, the meatballs will be very pale but still well flavoured from the cream gravy.
Serve with mashed potato or egg noodles. Lingonberry jam alongside is traditional.

Combine {{beef-mince}} of beef mince and {{pork-mince}} of pork mince in a bowl. Add {{breadcrumbs-fresh}} of fresh breadcrumbs, {{eggs}} egg, {{whole-milk}} of whole milk, {{onion-powder}} of onion powder, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt, and {{black-pepper-ground}} of pepper. Mix briefly. Shape into small balls, about 3 cm across.

Pour {{stock-beef}} of beef stock into the slow cooker. Stir in {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard and {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce. Lower the meatballs into the stock. Set to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours.
Switch the slow cooker to HIGH. Stir {{double-cream}} of double cream into the broth. Cook for 15 minutes until the sauce is thickened and cream-coloured. Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

rows.symptom: The meatballs are dense and tight
rows.cause: The mixture was overworked when forming.
rows.fix: Nothing can be done now. Next time mix only until just combined, and handle the mixture as little as possible.

rows.symptom: The cream sauce has split and looks grainy
rows.cause: The cream was added when the pot was at very high heat.
rows.fix: Stir vigorously; it may come back together. Add a splash of stock and stir. Next time reduce to LOW before adding cream.

rows.cause: The meatballs released a lot of liquid during cooking, diluting the cream.
rows.fix: Mix a tablespoon of cornflour with 2 tablespoons of cold water. Stir into the sauce and cook on HIGH for 5 minutes until thickened.

rows.cause: Not enough binding agent in the mix, or the meatballs were stirred too roughly during cooking.
rows.fix: Stir the meat into the cream sauce and serve as a ragu over noodles. Next time add a second egg and an extra tablespoon of breadcrumbs.

content.text: Swedish meatballs became one of the most recognised Nordic dishes outside Scandinavia. They are a staple of Swedish home cooking and are traditionally served at celebrations and family meals. The cream sauce and the two-meat mix are what distinguish them from other European meatball traditions. The slow cooker is a very practical way to make a large batch for a dinner party or a week of meals.
